name: Schur-Siegel-Smyth trace constant (C_86): improve either certified bound
compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days for finite polynomial and step or piecewise-linear density certificates with outward-rounded interval/ball verification; LP search over larger auxiliary-polynomial pools dominates.
statement: Let C_86 (also written lambda^{SSS}, constant 86a in Terence Tao's optimization-constants repository) be liminf tr(alpha)/deg(alpha) over all totally positive algebraic integers alpha; equivalently, the supremum of rho >= 0 such that all but finitely many totally positive algebraic integers satisfy tr(alpha) >= rho * deg(alpha). Schur proved C_86 >= sqrt(e) and Siegel proved C_86 >= 1.73361..., followed by Smyth's auxiliary-polynomial method up to 1.793145 (Wang-Wu-Wu). Orloski, Talebizadeh Sardari and Smith (Math. Comp. 94, 2025; arXiv:2401.03252) added a logarithmic-energy constraint to prove C_86 >= 1.80203. On the upper-bound side, Smith (Annals of Math. 200, 2024; arXiv:2111.12660) proved C_86 < 2, disproving the conjecture C_86 = 2, and Orloski and Talebizadeh Sardari (arXiv:2304.10021) gave a discretized primal measure construction proving C_86 <= 1.8216. Tao's live page on 2026-11-24 displays 1.80203 <= C_86 <= 1.8084990, listing Pinho's 1.8117251 (independently replayed by Toledo) and Koshta's 1.8084990 (independently replayed in merged teorth/optimizationproblems PR #292 by rozetyp and Canli, though page prose still retains an older asterisk remark). Open pull requests on teorth/optimizationproblems (#298 by R. Pinho at 1.8054939963*, using 31 primitive irreducible auxiliaries up to degree 21 — 11 with nonreal roots — on a 7,418-node continuous rational piecewise-linear density in rpinho/math-certificates; #270 by V. Patankar at 1.8054838*, using 37 auxiliaries on a 7,873-knot continuous rational piecewise-linear density in vidigoat/optimization-records; and #315 adding D. Niedbala Giraudin's arXiv:2609.29298 bound C_86 >= 1.80220) and November 2026 unrefereed Hexagon preprints (D. Niedbala Giraudin 2611.00275v1 at C_86 >= 1.8022246; T. S. Tomar 2611.00471v1 at 1.8022225 < C_86 < 1.8070809) claim tighter bounds. The exact value of C_86 remains open.
success_criterion: CONFIRMED by a rigorous, independently checkable strict improvement on either side (direction: lower bound max, upper bound min) over the best rigorous bound available at verification time after rechecking 86a.html, open pull requests on teorth/optimizationproblems, and recent arXiv/Hexagon preprints — or a rigorous proof of the exact value. (a) Lower bound: either (i) Smyth's auxiliary-function certificate giving finite non-constant integer polynomials Q with weights c_Q > 0 and certifying x - sum_Q c_Q log|Q(x)| >= b for all x > 0 in outward-rounded interval/ball arithmetic plus an explicit tail bound for large x; or (ii) an Orloski-Talebizadeh Sardari-Smith logarithmic-energy dual certificate (auxiliary density/measure plus integer polynomials with nonnegative weights) whose dual inequality on (0, infinity) is verified in outward-rounded interval/ball arithmetic with an explicit tail bound and whose derivation to C_86 >= b follows [OSS25] or is kernel-checked in Lean 4. (b) Upper bound: a compactly supported rational step density or continuous rational piecewise-linear density (or explicit measure with continuous logarithmic potential U_mu) mu on (0, infinity) of positive mass m = mu(R) > 0 and a finite set A of pairwise coprime primitive irreducible integer polynomials Q in Z[x] (roots may be real or nonreal; leading coefficients |lc(Q)| >= 1 included in |Q(x)|, so sign choices such as 1 - x vs x - 1 are equivalent) with positive rational weights b_Q > 0 satisfying Smith's Theorem 1.5 and Proposition 5.15 (arXiv:2111.12660): (1) each Q in A is a primitive irreducible polynomial in Z[x] (distinct up to sign), (2) sum_{Q in A} b_Q deg Q < m, (3) integral log|Q(x)| d mu(x) > 0 strictly for every Q in A, and (4) U_mu(x) - sum_{Q in A} b_Q log|Q(x)| >= 0 for all x in supp(mu) (certified by outward-rounded interval/ball bisection, extending to C by continuity of U_mu and the minimum principle since -log|Q(z)| -> +infinity at every real or nonreal root of Q outside supp(mu), with resultant integrality giving integral log|P| d mu >= 0 for all nonzero P in Z[x]), proving C_86 <= (1/m) integral x d mu(x). (c) Exact value: rigorous two-sided proof matching both bounds.
verification_method: For an upper bound: parse the rational step or continuous rational piecewise-linear density mu and polynomial set A; check each Q in A is primitive and irreducible over Q (pairwise coprime, without requiring real-only roots or +1 leading sign, while accounting for |lc(Q)| in log|Q|); recompute m = mu(R) > 0 and exact rational bound (1/m) integral x d mu(x); verify sum_{Q in A} b_Q deg Q < m; verify integral log|Q| d mu > 0 strictly for each Q in A in exact/outward-rounded ball arithmetic; and verify U_mu(x) - sum_{Q in A} b_Q log|Q(x)| >= 0 on supp(mu) (including cell endpoints) by rigorous interval/ball bisection. Calibrate against Pinho's 1.8117251 (noting 1 - x has leading coefficient -1), Koshta's 1.8084990, and piecewise-linear/complex-auxiliary certificates, and reject negative controls violating sum b_Q deg Q < m or integral log|Q| d mu > 0. For a lower bound: verify x - sum_Q c_Q log|Q(x)| >= b (or the OSS dual inequality) across (0, infinity) via outward-rounded interval bisection plus an explicit large-x tail bound, and audit the liminf derivation (finite exceptions permitted). Calibrate on Smyth's elementary polynomials and OSS 1.80203. Certificates exceeding 1 MB follow kit/SUBMIT.md section 1.
angles: Enlarge the auxiliary-polynomial pool beyond #270 (37 auxiliaries, 7,873 knots) and #298 (31 auxiliaries up to degree 21, 11 with nonreal roots, 7,418 nodes), including nonreal-root and nonmonic primitive irreducible auxiliaries allowed by Smith Proposition 5.15.

Discretize Smith's primal LP (minimize integral x d mu subject to integral log|Q| d mu >= eps) with adaptive piecewise-linear or step densities, refine cuts at local minima, rationalize with a safety margin, and certify via Arb/interval bisection.
On the lower side, pair the Orloski-Talebizadeh Sardari-Smith logarithmic-energy constraint with new auxiliary-polynomial families beyond Giraudin's 1.8022246.
pitfalls: Lower bound versus upper bound: lower bounds use Smyth/OSS dual inequalities, while upper bounds use explicit feasible measures under Smith's sufficiency criterion. A certificate for one direction proves nothing about the other.
C_86 is a liminf (holding for all but finitely many totally positive algebraic integers), not an absolute minimum over all totally positive algebraic integers.
Smith's upper-bound criterion requires integral log|Q| d mu > 0 strictly (with positive rational weights b_Q > 0 and sum b_Q deg Q < m); boundary zero values fail the theorem.

Smith's Proposition 5.15 does not require auxiliary polynomials Q in A to have real roots or leading coefficient +1 (provided |lc(Q)| is included in log|Q| and U_mu is continuous); Pinho's 1.8117251 calibration certificate already includes 1 - x (leading coefficient -1), and #298 uses 11 auxiliaries with nonreal roots.
Tao's rendered 86a.html page lags open pull requests (#298, #270, #315) and November 2026 preprints; recheck both the page and open PRs immediately before claiming.
The retracted 2016 paper of Pratt, Shakan and Zaharescu (J. Math. Anal. Appl. 436, retracted 2023) still appears in searches; never cite it.
